_comment: Manual audit of the unanswerable arm (10 questions), read by run_guardrails.py when writing reports/w47-guardrails.md. Reason: the regex refusal classifier is coarse in both directions — it misses 'hedged hallucinations' (a model that opens with 'the context does not include X' and then answers from memory anyway) and it fires on substantive answers that merely contain a caveat sentence. n=10 is small enough to read every answer.

q005.note: naive: 'context does not include PCI DSS v4.0' and stops. Correct.

q019.note: naive: no ISO/IEC 27001 text, stops. Correct.

q020.note: naive hedges ('cannot be determined') then supplies VND 100,000,000 from memory — exactly the failure mode a guardrail exists for.

q044.note: naive answers the DORA register question in full from outside knowledge, no hedge.

q045.note: naive: 'context covers EU GDPR/AI Act, not UK DPA' then gives £17.5m / 4% anyway.

q046.note: naive: CPRA 45 days + 45-day extension, no hedge at all.

q047.note: naive: SOC 2 PI1.1–PI1.5 listed as fact.

q048.note: naive: no ISO/IEC 42001 text, stops. Correct.

q049.note: naive: no PSD3 timeline in context, stops. Correct.

q050.note: naive hedges ('does not specify') then asserts 'It only states that for FedRAMP Moderate, the CSP must…' — attributes outside knowledge to the context.

q003.note: only Annex III item 2 retrieved, the request needs the whole list — refusing is defensible.

q012.note: gold section is a retrieval miss for hybrid (see w47-retrieval-40q.md) — nothing to ground on.

q015.note: classifier false positive: substantive answer that also contains a 'what is missing' caveat.

q018.note: classifier false positive: answered with [ai_act#art26-p1] plus a caveat sentence.
